content: CIB1, also known as Calcium and Integrin-Binding Protein 1, is a protein in humans that is encoded by the CIB1 gene. This protein belongs to the family of calcium-binding proteins. While its precise biological function has not yet been fully elucidated, it is known to interact with DNA-dependent protein kinase (DNA-PK). This interaction suggests that CIB1 may play a role in the regulation of kinase and phosphatase activities involved in DNA end-joining processes. Additionally, CIB1 interacts with integrin alpha(IIb)beta(3), which indicates that it may function as a regulatory molecule for this specific integrin. This interaction could have implications in cellular adhesion and signaling processes mediated by integrins. CIB1 has also been demonstrated to interact with several other proteins, including RAC3, PSEN2 (Presenilin-2), DNA-PKcs (the catalytic subunit of DNA-dependent protein kinase), UBR5 (a ubiquitin ligase), and CD61 (also known as integrin beta-3). These interactions suggest that CIB1 may have diverse roles in cellular signaling, protein regulation, and possibly in pathological processes.
